summary: A .gitignore file lists files and folders Git should not track, such as cache folders, logs, and passwords.
notes: Commit .gitignore so everyone working on the project ignores the same files.
*.log ignores every file that ends in .log, in any folder.
Never commit passwords or API keys. Put them in a file that .gitignore lists.
pitfall: .gitignore does not affect files Git already tracks. If you committed debug.log before, it keeps showing as modified. Run git rm --cached debug.log and commit to stop tracking it.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with one commit, plus two new untracked items: a __pycache__ folder and debug.log.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
